pr_body:
Rework of the `cmd::FlattenLayers` implementation to accomodate the 'Merge Down' command as a special case. Fix #4468.

This includes a multitude of changes and additions to said implementation, listed below. Because not all of these modifications are directly related to the linked issue, feedback on what could be improved or skipped altogether would be greatly appreciated.

Summary of changes:
- Resetting of cel opacity for the destination layer, as well as the layer's visibility, opacity and blend mode, in cases where flattening is done onto an existing layer rather than a new one.
- Unconditional use of `shrink_bounds` to ensure layer edges are displayed correctly.
- Swapped the usage of `CopyRect` command for a `ReplaceImage`. This was done merely because I could not get the former to work properly when flattening onto an existing, non-background layer.
- Changed the boolean `newBlend` parameter of `cmd::FlattenLayers` (and the `m_newBlendMethod` member variable) for an integer `options` and `m_options` respectively, to enable and disable behaviours (defined in the `cmd::FlattenLayers::Options` enum) through a single bitmask value. These options are:
  - `NewBlendMethod`: identical to `newBlend`.
  - `Inplace`: utilize the last layer in the provided list as destination for flattening rather than spawning a new layer to flatten onto. Similar to utilizing the background layer.
  - `MergeDown`: invoke `notifyLayerMergedDown` before issuing the removal of source layers.
  - `ExtendCanvas`: give a larger size to the temporary image being rendered to, when cels in a frame are partially or completely outside of the canvas. Without this option, pixels outside of those bounds are discarded.
- All three of the new options detailed above are enabled when `cmd::FlattenLayers` is invoked through `MergeDownLayerCommand`. When invoked through `FlattenLayersCommand`, the new options are ignored altogether, thus retaining the behaviour prior to this rework, save for the resetting of visibility, opacity and blend mode, and the adjusting of layer edges.

I've left note of a few smaller details via comments in the code itself, mostly to explain what exactly a series of lines are doing. Please, let me know if any of them are too redundant.
pr_comments:
Hi @dacap! A note about adjusting the z-index, both changing and not changing the value can affect the final image in different scenarios. Setting it to zero on the destination could give a similar result if there's a cel below it with a z-index greater than zero, for instance:

```
// Before merging
(layer 2)  [Z:0] <-- source
(layer 1)  [Z:1] <-- destination, rendered on top
(layer 0)  [Z:1] <-- layer below destination

// After merging
(merged)   [Z:0] <-- destination
(layer 0)  [Z:1] <-- layer below, rendered on top
```

This means some edge cases are unsolvable too (cannot preserve the exact same final image without outright flattening everything) when more than two layers are involved. I'm not sure what could be done.

Anyway, setting the z-index to zero, as if a new cel was created, would be consistent with opacity and blend mode being reset back to the default, so that may be the more predictable behaviour.

That's right. I think setting the z-index to 0 is the simplest way to approach this.

There is that (solvable) edge case where the resulting layer after a merge down should have an adjusted z-index (to be on top of a specific layer), but I don't think it's worth it. It's already working a lot better than the current `main`.

It works great @Liebranca! I'll merge it as it is, there is a minor memory overhead now that we use `ReplaceImage` instead of `CopyRect`, but as [I mentioned](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/pull/4643#discussion_r1752237044) it's something we can address in the future.

issue_context.title: Merge layers taking into account z-index
issue_context.body:
When a user merge layers the resulting layer should be created taking into account the z-index of the merged layers.

Originally reported here:
https://community.aseprite.org/t/merge-with-z-index/22106
comments: The draft in 3b217b7 fixes the bug in the immediate sense, but I have some concerns about whether the way opacity is handled achieves the intended effect, so I want to take a closer look at that next. After reading `app/cmd/flatten_layers.cpp` I'm left thinking perhaps reusing some of that logic would be simpler in the end, but I'm not entirely sure.

> I'm left thinking perhaps reusing some of that logic would be simpler in the end, but I'm not entirely sure

It seems to me that a "merge down" is a special case of a "flatten layers" with only two layers selected, but when more layers are selected the solution gets tricky (that's why FlattenLayers just creates a new layer to simplify the impl).

Probably we can modify `FlattenLayers` to improve this special case with a similar impl to "merge down" (and finally merge down could just use `cmd::FlattenLayers`).

I've been working on `cmd::FlattenLayers` in a [separate branch](https://github.com/Liebranca/aseprite/blob/aa52299ba539a01f36f7959ec3f052e0e53a4177/src/app/cmd/flatten_layers.cpp) these last few days. Because producing the final image through `renderSprite` fixes the issue already, I went ahead and looked at some other things around it.

My idea was addressing __similar__ problems I noticed, that caused the result of the merge to look different to the original image in cases where both should be visually identical. Tried to fix whatever I found slightly odd while I was at it, may have gone too far in some places.

In summary:

- Changed the bool parameter for an int, so that I could pass multiple switches with one value.
- Made it so layers can be flattened "in-place", that is, overwriting the destination layer rather than spawning a new one.
- Modified the temporary image so that I could render outside the canvas. May be redundant in some cases. I went for bit of a bruteforce approach with this one, it can probably be improved.
- Changed the `onExecute` loop to always `shrink_bounds` so layer edges display properly. This one may also be redundant in some cases.
- Experimented with having z-index account for the removal of the source layers, to avoid having cels "pop" through once these layers are deleted. Doesn't work in some cases, so I have to rethink it a bit.
- Made it so opacity and blend mode are reset when flattening in-place. This is just a small detail, but it always confuses me when it isn't there.

Anyway, I have to review and clean things up, but it works. Sometime later I'd like to test if merging groups is viable with this implementation, I'm thinking it should be.

@Liebranca I'll take a look to your branch (I've rebased it [here](https://github.com/dacap/aseprite/tree/experimental-flatten-layers) to `main` removing the merge commit). Anyway it might be better to create a PR in draft mode to review it.
